milestone.name: Provenance-safe project updates
milestone.objective: Deliver a validated, provenance-aware, transactional project updater while preserving local customization and requiring exact approval for risky dispositions.

lastCompletedWork.summary: Prepared a 37-file, unstaged and uncommitted candidate for the completed safe updater implementation after full validation and an independent no-findings review rerun.

decisions.decision: Treat the safe updater as implementation-complete and candidate-ready, with handoff status waiting-approval.
decisions.rationale: STEP-013 prepared the validated candidate, but no approval has been granted to create a local commit.

decisions.decision: Use normalized manifest 1.1 and lock 1.0 provenance with all, additive, and select planning modes.
decisions.rationale: The updater now classifies managed state from normalized baselines and closes selected work over dependencies and generated companions.

decisions.decision: Support track, pin, and fork policies plus keep, replace, fork, and remove dispositions without a force-all option.
decisions.rationale: Risk acceptance is exact and selection-bound; exact-force applies only to explicitly reviewed assets.

decisions.decision: Require transactional apply, exact rollback, and journaled recovery for modern and legacy migration paths.
decisions.rationale: Manifest-lock cutover, local customization, fork creation, generated companions, and interrupted writes must remain recoverable without silent data loss.

decisions.decision: Preserve P4 release assurance as historical blocked lineage and LIVE-CHAT-001 as a separate planning-required initiative.
decisions.rationale: The safe updater workflow neither completes nor cancels unrelated release assurance, and no Live Chat implementation or Azure work occurred.

plannedInitiatives.name: Live Chat Interaction
plannedInitiatives.target: Reusable product capability, prototyped in C:\repos\skills-orchestrator-demo
plannedInitiatives.objective: Let a user ask what the application can do, receive a guided feature walkthrough, and continue asking grounded questions by text or voice.
firstVersion: A visible assistant entry point with text input, microphone control, transcript review, and optional spoken responses.
Deterministic capability cards and guided walkthroughs for reliable onboarding.
Freeform answers grounded only in approved product documentation and capability metadata, with source links and explicit unknowns.
Read-only behavior by default; any future action requires separate authorization and explicit user confirmation.
Graceful text-only and guided-only fallback when model or Speech services are unavailable.
architectureConstraints: Use AzureUSGovernment only for cloud model or Speech processing.
Run azure-discovery before selecting a region, model, Speech resource, quota, or deployment topology.
Keep credentials out of the browser; use a server-side boundary and managed identity for deployed Azure access.
Treat retrieved content and model output as untrusted; defend against prompt injection, unsupported claims, data leakage, and excessive agency.
Do not send microphone audio or transcripts to a cloud service until the user has clear notice and the applicable approval and privacy requirements are satisfied.
Do not create resources, incur cost, deploy, publish, commit, or push from this planning record.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can discover capabilities without knowing commands or feature names.
Users can complete at least one guided walkthrough and ask contextual follow-up questions.
Voice input exposes listening, transcript, correction, cancellation, permission-denied, and unavailable-service states.
Answers remain grounded, cite their product source, distinguish unknowns, and never claim an unavailable capability.
Keyboard-only, screen-reader, reduced-motion, responsive, and text-only experiences remain functional.
Security, privacy, latency, cost, failure-mode, and evaluation evidence pass before deployment approval is requested.
openDecisions: Which Azure Government model and Speech capabilities are currently available in the selected subscription and region?
What product documents form the authoritative grounding corpus and how are versions refreshed?
Should spoken responses default off, and what retention policy applies to transcripts?
What latency, answer-quality, accessibility, and cost thresholds define demo and production readiness?
Should the initial prototype remain informational or support separately confirmed product actions?

historicalLineage.name: P4 release assurance
historicalLineage.summary: Release assurance remains blocked by trusted signing, distinct independent review, restricted artifact distribution, installation-health evidence, tested revocation, and production verification. The safe updater workflow did not complete or cancel this lineage.

validation.evidence: Manifest 1.1 and lock 1.0 normalized provenance; all, additive, and select planning; track, pin, and fork policy; keep, replace, fork, and remove dispositions; exact-force without force-all; transactional apply, rollback, and recovery; legacy migration and security hardening; and operator documentation are complete through STEP-013.
STEP-009-DEFECT-001 was fixed: manifests requiring a newer minimum updater runtime now fail closed, while older compatible minimums remain accepted.

The review found five defects; all five received focused red-green repairs covering persisted fork recognition, runtime lock validation, option rejection, exact fork restoration and rollback, and documentation evidence consistency.
reports/change-review.json records no findings after the five repairs and additional adversarial generated-scope and framework-fork-reference coverage.

npm run check completed 173 total tests: 172 passed, 0 failed, and 1 expected skip; 274 files were security-scanned, 183 release files were checksum-verified, and all 47 skills were inventoried, audited, and distribution-verified.

The 37 candidate files are unstaged and uncommitted on release/1.1.2 at ad3e73cb19a645bccdedfc0ffa781976d98b31a8; the local origin/release/1.1.2 tracking ref remains at the same old commit because no push or fetch occurred.
No Azure work, deployment, publication, commit, push, pull request, release, or network operation occurred in this workflow.

worktree.attribution: The validated implementation boundary contains 37 files. STEP-014 adds synchronized continuity and terminal state reports; all remain unstaged and uncommitted pending separate commit approval.

blockers: Creating the local candidate commit requires explicit operator approval.
pendingApprovals: First: explicit operator approval to create local commit feat: add provenance-safe project updates.
Separately after a local commit: push requires its own approval and is not included in the commit approval.
Pull request, merge, release, publication, deployment, and any Azure or other external mutation each remain separately gated.
LIVE-CHAT-001 implementation requires an approved workflow plan; Azure Government discovery and any later provisioning or billable use remain separately gated.
limitations: This handoff does not stage, commit, push, publish, release, deploy, contact Azure, use the network, or advance current-execution-state.json or execution-log.jsonl.
The local remote-tracking ref is only local evidence of the last known remote state; no network refresh was authorized.
P4 release assurance remains historical blocked lineage, not completed or cancelled.
LIVE-CHAT-001 remains a separate planning-required initiative and has not been implemented.
